question.problem:
Written in **ascending order**, the solutions to $|6-k|=2$ are $k=${{field-1}} and $k=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|6-k|=6-k,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|6-k| & =2 \\ 6-k & =2 \\ -k & =-4 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|6-k|=-(6-k),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|6-k| & =2 \\ -(6-k) & =2 \\ -6+k & =2 \\ k & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $k=4$ and $k=8.$
